## Intended use
Refined reusable environmental design candidate for the Hall of Blood, correcting only the captive's architectural scale while retaining the successful chamber baseline.

## Edit source — provider input image 1
hall-of-blood-environment-canonical-candidate-1-1.png (366302c5-7cd2-49c5-9992-f306eefd5033). This is the image to edit.

## Desired edited result
Retain the existing wide elevated establishing composition and the successful Hall of Blood architecture, but rescale M’uru substantially smaller so the naaru fits naturally inside the chamber's central containment zone. M’uru should hover low above the circular dais and read as approximately a few blood-elf heights rather than a monumental figure spanning the central bay. Preserve M’uru’s complete canonical silhouette and component arrangement at the reduced scale. Redirect the fixed crimson extraction beams so they converge accurately on the smaller captive. Reconstruct the space vacated by the oversized figure as coherent distant arches, columns, shadow, warm haze, and architectural depth matching the existing room. Keep the central dais, radial floor conduits, containment pylons, platforms, stairs, foreground columns, tiny attendants, viewpoint, and overall room layout intact. The chamber must remain the primary subject and M’uru a contained focal landmark within it.

## Continuity priorities
Preserve the existing Hall of Blood's broad circular plan, elevated entrance viewpoint, foreground framing columns, red-black-gold Thalassian architecture, patterned ceiling, curved walls, pointed openings, raised platforms, central recessed dais, radial floor network, fixed pylons, navigable walkways, tiny scale figures, dark oppressive palette, and painterly Warcraft finish. Preserve the canonical M’uru design from the supplied reference: exact faceless naaru silhouette, relative component arrangement, violet crystalline structures, white-gold core, rose-magenta radiance, and suspended symmetry. Preserve the architectural scale established by the people and railings; do not enlarge those elements to compensate.

## Composition after edit
Same wide square establishing view and architectural framing as the source. The room remains dominant. Place the smaller M’uru on the central vertical axis just above the dais, with ample visible chamber volume around and above it. Binding beams form restrained diagonals from the existing pylons to the reduced captive. Maintain clear circulation paths and layered depth.

## Purposeful use of space after edit
Unless the brief explicitly calls for a sparse, minimalist, isolated-study, or open-field composition, concentrate quiet negative space only in explicit text-reservation regions. Everywhere else, make each area contribute to subject, setting, atmosphere, depth, scale, motion, focus, or visual flow without adding clutter. Atmospheric open space is purposeful when it clearly establishes mood or scale; avoid large unmotivated blank areas and do not invent a text landing zone where none was requested.

## Lighting and mood after edit
Maintain blackened wine red, dark plum, charcoal, tarnished gold, muted amber, and crimson apparatus light. M’uru remains a bright white-gold, rose-magenta, and violet focal light, but its bloom should be contained locally rather than flooding or overpowering the whole chamber. Magnificent, secretive, controlled, sorrowful, and morally oppressive.

## Reference image roles (actual provider input order)
Provider input image 2: canonical identity for the smaller M’uru within the Hall of Blood. Preserve: Complete faceless naaru silhouette, relative component arrangement, violet crystalline structures, white-gold central core, rose-magenta glow, suspended symmetry, and painterly finish.. Must change: Reduce M’uru to an environmental scale of only a few blood-elf heights, hover it low above the central dais, add localized containment beams, and replace the isolated portrait background with the existing Hall of Blood architecture.. Image id: b0aa92d9-7b93-42ce-9c68-8788b0f9aaa2.

## Additional constraints and exclusions
This is a scale correction, not an architectural redesign. M’uru must be much smaller than in the source and visibly contained by the room. Do not replace the chamber, change the viewpoint, add a giant cage, add chains, or turn the scene into a shrine. No focal named characters, combat, readable text, labels, interface elements, logos, signatures, or watermarks. Keep an illustrated painterly finish rather than glossy 3D rendering.

## Rendered-text policy
Do not render words, letters, numbers, captions, labels, signatures, watermarks, logos, or story copy. Keep all story text as editable Lorekeeper text outside the raster image.

## Output target and protected regions
Raster size: 1024x1024. Aspect ratio: 1:1.

## Edit discipline
Make the requested revision as one coherent image. Preserve the explicitly listed continuity priorities, but do not freeze every unmentioned pixel or secondary detail. Allow nearby pose, framing, lighting, background, texture, and geometry to adapt naturally when needed to integrate the edit. Keep unrelated major subjects and story facts recognizable without duplicating, deforming, or partially reconstructing them.

images.altText: Wide painterly view of the underground Hall of Blood, where radiant violet-and-gold M’uru hangs above a recessed circular dais amid curved red-black Silvermoon architecture and converging crimson extraction beams.
images.prompt:
## Intended use
Exploratory canonical environment-design candidate for the Hall of Blood, establishing the hidden Silvermoon holding chamber where M’uru is confined and its Light is extracted. This is reusable location concept art, not a cover or book-page composition.

## Scene and background
A wide establishing view inside the underground Hall of Blood. M’uru hangs suspended above a recessed circular containment dais at the far-center of a broad curved chamber. A controlled network of fixed magisterial pylons and conduits projects taut crimson-red binding and extraction beams into the naaru, while channels in the floor carry red-gold energy outward. The architecture and apparatus make the imprisonment and forced use immediately legible.

## Subjects
The Hall of Blood as the primary subject; M’uru as its central captive landmark. No focal named characters. Any distant attendants or guards, if present for scale, remain tiny indistinct silhouettes subordinate to the environment.

## Appearance and continuity anchors
Faithfully preserve M’uru’s approved canonical form, silhouette, violet crystalline components, white-gold core, rose-magenta radiance, and suspended symmetry. Establish the Hall of Blood as a broad circular or oval subterranean Silvermoon chamber with massive dark wine-red columns, sweeping curved walls, high patterned ceiling, gold-edged arches, pointed inset openings, layered perimeter walkways, raised monitoring platforms, restricted entrances, and a central recessed containment floor. The apparatus is elegant but coercive Thalassian engineering: blackened red metal, dark stone, gold trim, crimson crystal nodes, controlled runic channels, and fixed siphoning pylons integrated into the architecture.

## Action
M’uru remains suspended and constrained at the center while several stable red extraction beams draw Light into the surrounding containment network. The chamber is active but orderly, more controlled laboratory-prison than chaotic ritual.

## Expression, pose, and gaze
M’uru is faceless and non-humanoid, held in solemn ordered suspension; its symmetry is subtly strained by the surrounding binding force. No theatrical attack pose.

## Setting and environment
Hidden underground beneath Silvermoon in the Hall of Blood. A monumental enclosed chamber with controlled access, deep peripheral shadow, raised side platforms, curved circulation paths, and architecture based on the supplied in-game room screenshot. The room should feel designed around containment, monitoring, calibration, and distribution rather than worship.

## Style, medium, and palette
Polished hand-painted Warcraft fantasy illustration matching the approved project studies and Wretched style target: layered digital paint, visible broken brush texture, varied and sometimes lost edges, selective crisp architectural and magical details, painterly color transitions, stylized Warcraft proportions, and rich modeling without glossy 3D-render smoothness. Palette: blackened wine red, dark plum, charcoal, tarnished gold, muted amber, and crimson apparatus light, contrasted by M’uru’s sacred white-gold, rose-magenta, and violet radiance.

## Camera and framing
Wide landscape environmental concept, viewed from a slightly elevated three-quarter position near the chamber entrance or perimeter walkway. Show the room’s breadth, curved plan, central recessed dais, surrounding platforms, columns, ceiling sweep, and at least one controlled approach route. M’uru is fully visible at the compositional center but small enough that the architecture remains the primary subject.

## Composition
Strong architectural framing from foreground columns and walkway edges guides the eye toward M’uru at the far-center. The circular dais and radial conduits organize the chamber. Binding beams create restrained diagonals that converge on the captive. Use deep occupied shadows and atmospheric depth rather than broad empty areas; no reserved text zone.

## Purposeful use of space
Unless the brief explicitly calls for a sparse, minimalist, isolated-study, or open-field composition, concentrate quiet negative space only in explicit text-reservation regions. Everywhere else, make each area contribute to subject, setting, atmosphere, depth, scale, motion, focus, or visual flow without adding clutter. Atmospheric open space is purposeful when it clearly establishes mood or scale; avoid large unmotivated blank areas and do not invent a text landing zone where none was requested.

## Lighting and mood
M’uru provides sacred white-gold and rose-violet illumination while the extraction network answers with harsher crimson and red-gold light. Faint amber architectural lamps define access paths. Mood: magnificent, secretive, controlled, morally oppressive, and sorrowful—blood elf splendor turned into an instrument of survival.

## Reference image roles (actual provider input order)
Provider input image 1: authoritative architecture and room-shape baseline for the Hall of Blood. Preserve: Broad curved chamber, massive dark columns, red-black-gold Silvermoon materials, high decorated ceiling, pointed openings, raised side platforms, perimeter circulation, central containment zone, and integrated red magical extraction beams.. Must change: Replace the in-game camera, low-detail geometry, player/NPC figures, interface-like presentation, and cropped M’uru with a coherent wide painterly environment study. Clarify spatial layout and containment infrastructure.. Image id: 84429164-88a7-4e60-b9ae-cd0a71f233ca.
Provider input image 2: canonical identity for M’uru. Preserve: M’uru’s complete faceless naaru silhouette, relative component arrangement, violet crystalline surfaces, white-gold central core, rose-magenta glow, and suspended symmetry.. Must change: Place M’uru farther away within the chamber at environmental scale, visibly constrained by integrated extraction beams. Replace the neutral portrait framing and abstract background with the Hall of Blood establishing view.. Image id: b0aa92d9-7b93-42ce-9c68-8788b0f9aaa2.
Provider input image 3: approved project rendering and finish reference. Preserve: Layered hand-painted Warcraft illustration finish, broken color, varied edges, selective crispness, dark warm atmosphere, stylized rich modeling, and non-photoreal painterly surfaces.. Must change: Do not depict Falanaras or copy his armor, weapon, anatomy, pose, or portrait composition. Apply the rendering language to the environment.. Image id: a22d39de-1219-4f9b-8475-2aab8132460d.
Provider input image 4: original project style target for painterly handling. Preserve: Visible digital brushwork, selective focal detail, softer peripheral edges, stylized Warcraft visual language, atmospheric depth, and an illustrated rather than rendered finish.. Must change: Do not copy the Wretched creature, icy setting, armor palette, or action composition. Translate only the paint handling and edge hierarchy into the Hall of Blood.. Image id: 4a08dea9-b7bb-4e28-8712-bf672b4e9d2c.

## Constraints and exclusions
Use the room screenshot as architectural and spatial baseline, not as a composition to copy. Use the approved M’uru image as exact identity reference. Preserve the established painterly project style. The chamber must read as Silvermoon/Thalassian rather than generic dungeon, cathedral, industrial factory, or demonic lair. Do not add chains wrapped around M’uru; restraint is expressed through integrated magical beams, pylons, and field apparatus. Avoid a giant cage of iron bars. No close focal characters, combat, interface elements, labels, readable runes, text, logos, signatures, or watermarks. Keep all architecture coherent and navigable, with believable platforms and access routes.

## Creative latitude
Meet every stated story, continuity, composition, and output requirement. Freely compose visual details that are not prescribed by the brief or references so the result feels intentional and coherent. Do not infer that unspecified details are forbidden, and do not add literal exclusions such as 'nothing else'.

## Rendered-text policy
Do not render words, letters, numbers, captions, labels, signatures, watermarks, logos, or story copy. Keep all story text as editable Lorekeeper text outside the raster image.

## Output target and protected regions
Raster size: 1024x1024. Aspect ratio: 1:1.
